latest.title: Coaching an Engineer Through a Production Incident Without Taking Over
latest.description: The fastest way to resolve a production incident is usually to take it over yourself. If you have more experience with the system, you can often shortcut straight to the likely cause and fix it faster than someone still building that intuition. That instinct is correct in the moment and wrong as a habit, because it trains the other engineer to hand you anything that gets hard, instead of building the judgment to handle it themselves next time.

latest.title: Why Autoscaling Alone Isn't Enough for Predictable Traffic Events
latest.description: Autoscaling on EKS has gotten genuinely good. HPA reacts to load, Karpenter provisions nodes fast, and for the majority of traffic patterns that's the right design: don't pay for capacity you don't need, let the system react to demand as it arrives. Most of the time, reactive scaling is correct scaling.
